svg.title: Launching a VAR Motion That Pays
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-var-launch-sequence; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: Launching a VAR Motion That Pays; subtitle: License as entry ticket, services as the profit layer; caption: Operators sequence a VAR motion from proven direct sales through published implementation ballparks, a full license stack, transparent quoting and go-live tracking.; assumptions note: Step order follows the operator gates in Chapter Q1. No durations or margins are added beyond those stated by the cited practitioners.; note: Sources: Phil Morettini [L1YsH5QkIus @ 00:02:18]; Channel Marketing Academy [vLO0gA3TgxE @ 00:01:38]; Stuart Sutton [yasPH-UlTQo @ 00:08:10]; Ben Fox of TC2 via Staying Connected [BJPNVL1CIiM @ 00:04:10]; Summer Zaldivar [4qYKEjVIAjc @ 00:00:36].; stages: step: 01; label: Prove direct sales first; value: Step 1; detail: Phil Morettini: no one can sell your product if you cannot, and VARs will not create demand for a vendor.; step: 02; label: Publish implementation ballparks; value: Step 2; detail: Entry, medium and heavy ballparks such as a month and a half, six months and two years; a $50,000 surprise on a $5,000 buyer embarrasses the VAR.; step: 03; label: Stack setup, minimum and usage fees; value: Step 3; detail: Stuart Sutton layers setup fees, monthly minimums, usage pricing and per-hour customization; the minimum covers subscribers whose usage falls below the cost of cutting an invoice.; step: 04; label: Break out markup and tax lines; value: Step 4; detail: Ben Fox has seen a 60 percent OEM discount passed through as 58 percent, and customs and import fees disguised as taxes.; step: 05; label: Track go-live and active users; value: Step 5; detail: Summer Zaldivar: of 20 at-risk high-volume customers, eight were remediated via premier support, saving over 250,000 and lifting renewal rate by 5 percent.
